clue.text: A chap started to enjoy being home

parts.note: bod is informal British slang for a person or chap

indicators.note: started points to where the word enjoy begins, so take its first letter

explanation.surface: A man was beginning to enjoy staying at home.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling, the place where someone lives.

clue.text: Personal tax outwardly ripe for change

indicators.note: outwardly says the reworked letters sit on the outside, wrapping the tax word
for change asks for the letters of ripe to be changed into a new order

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: A personal tax that is, on the face of it, ripe for reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' makes PRIE, and 'outwardly' sets it around the tax; VAT is value added tax, Britain's sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Private and personal both describe what belongs to one individual rather than the public.

clue.text: Give birth at Paddington?

definitions.meaning: to give birth to a child
Paddington is the famous children's-book ... from Peru, found at the London railway station

explanation.definitionFit: To bear a child is to deliver it, and Paddington is a fictional bear, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Brought up to date when reds in demo rerouted

indicators.note: rerouted sends the letters of reds in demo along a different path, a new order

explanation.surface: A protest march updated after the communists' route was changed.
explanation.definitionFit: To modernise something is to update it to current standards.

clue.text: Professional soldier in uniform

definitions.meaning: a full-time career soldier, not a reservist
uniform as an adjective means even, the same throughout

explanation.definitionFit: A career soldier in the standing army is termed a regular, and regular also means even or consistent.

clue.text: A crowd of pilots left at last

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is where British military pilots serve

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word left

explanation.surface: A bunch of airmen finally departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft of things is informal for a large number or collection.

clue.text: Grandmother's eaten nothing — complain

indicators.note: eaten means the zero has been swallowed, so it goes inside the grandmother word

parts.note: gran is a familiar name for a grandmother; the 's stands for has
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Granny has eaten nothing and grumbles about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To groan is to moan or grumble audibly.

clue.text: Dog that might stagger?

definitions.meaning: a breed of crossbred hunting dog
a person who lurches, staggering about, could be called one who lurches

explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a greyhound-cross hunting dog, and to lurch is to stagger, so one who lurches fits the playful second reading.

clue.text: First principles? Turns out to protect us coin

indicators.note: to protect means the reworked letters surround and shield the coin
out means the letters of turns are put out of order

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction about shielding American money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes RUNTS, which 'to protect' wraps around the coin. 'us coin' reads as us plus a coin, but it is a US coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudiments are the basic elements of a subject, its first principles.

clue.text: City pub started catering, and serving no ale!

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place

indicators.note: started takes the first letter of catering
serving here works the letters of no ale into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A city pub has begun offering food but sells no beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is a large city in Catalonia, Spain.

clue.text: Baffled by empty rifle found in overflow

indicators.note: found in places the rifle remnant inside the overflow word

parts.note: a flood is an overflow of water

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of rifle, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Puzzled by an unloaded gun lying in floodwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outside letters of rifle; 'found in' places them inside the overflow word.
explanation.definitionFit: Floored is informal for stumped or completely bewildered.

clue.text: Bloke on plunger going a different way

indicators.note: on places the bloke word after the plunger word in an across answer

parts.note: a diver plunges into water
gent, short for gentleman, means a man or bloke

explanation.surface: A man riding a plunger heads off in another direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Divergent paths separate and move apart from each other.

clue.text: The air of a worker on the edge?

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker in crosswords
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A question about the bearing of a labourer standing at the brink.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a song or tune, and air is an old word for a melody.

clue.text: Egg producer backing an agent for colouring

parts.note: a hen lays eggs

indicators.note: backing means the word an is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A chicken supporting a spy for colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agent' looks like a spy to be backed, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye made from a plant, used to colour hair and skin.

clue.text: Tried to get rid of a number of animals

indicators.note: to get rid of tells us the letter a is dropped from the tried word

parts.note: a court case that has been heard has been tried

explanation.surface: Attempted to dispose of some livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried' looks like 'attempted', but it means judged in court, as a case that has been heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of cattle or similar animals.

clue.text: Dave rang at work — that's innovative!

indicators.note: at work means the letters of dave rang at are busily rearranged

explanation.surface: A colleague phoned the office with a new idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde describes experimental, pioneering work ahead of its time.

clue.text: A bit of tranquillity, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals a word said out loud that matches another in sound

parts.note: peace is calm or tranquillity

explanation.surface: Requesting a little calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or fragment of something.

clue.text: Views crop pests as destructive

indicators.note: as destructive asks for the letters of crop pests to be broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A farmer's outlook on harmful insects in the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospects are views or outlooks, as from a high point.

clue.text: Experienced doctor managed to overcome disease at last

indicators.note: to overcome places the managed word beyond the disease letter, finishing the run

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of disease

parts.note: ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: A seasoned physician eventually beat the illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long experience in a field.

clue.text: Nato advisor discovered to be a vile sort of chap

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, so the letters lie exposed inside nato advisor

explanation.surface: A NATO consultant is exposed as a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad is an insult for a loathsome, contemptible person.

clue.text: Resort that's not fashionable in part of Iberia

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the fashionable word out of the Iberian country

parts.note: Spain occupies most of the Iberian peninsula
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A holiday spot in Iberia that is out of vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a health resort, often with mineral springs.

clue.text: Nearly open with composition for two — no time to be late

indicators.note: nearly means the open word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden

indicators.note: no removes the time letter from the music word

parts.note: a duet is music for two performers

explanation.surface: Nearly ready to perform a duet but without time, so running behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' trims OVERT to OVER; 'no time' drops T from DUET to leave DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means past its expected time, behind schedule.

clue.text: Proposal to support last move with feeling

indicators.note: to support in a down answer puts the proposal word beneath, holding up the letter above
last picks the final letter of move

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A suggestion backing the final manoeuvre with passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotion is a strong feeling such as joy or anger.

clue.text: Gather that mother's on board a ship

indicators.note: on board places mother inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
ma is mother; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Collect that mum is aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to accumulate or collect a large quantity.

clue.text: Approaches a place for meeting on Sunday

parts.note: a venue is where a meeting is held

explanation.surface: Ways in to a meeting place on Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are ways in or methods of approach.

clue.text: Went out with father Ted

parts.note: da is a familiar word for father
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dated a priest named Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father Ted' suggests the TV sitcom priest, but father here is just a familiar word for a dad.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dated someone is to have gone out with them romantically.

clue.text: Cue for a walk by the seaside and a pint?

parts.note: a prom, short for promenade, is a seafront walkway in British resorts
PT is the abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: A suggestion of a seafront stroll and a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt is a cue or reminder given to an actor.

clue.text: This girl exercises with a heartless rival

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle of rival, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A girl works out with an uncaring competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Perfect! I would get better in east London

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would

indicators.note: in east London the Cockney accent drops the initial H

parts.note: to heal is to make better

explanation.surface: Delighted at getting well in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in east London' means Cockney speech, which drops the H, so HEAL becomes 'EAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means flawless, exactly as wished.

clue.text: 10 followed outside, subdued

indicators.note: outside puts the pursued word around the number

parts.note: chased means pursued or followed
10 is ten

explanation.surface: Pursued round the outside, humbled.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to clue 10 but is simply the number TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastened means humbled or restrained after a rebuke.

clue.text: Cover a bed found outside

indicators.note: found outside puts the bed word around the letter a

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A blanket for a bed discovered out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat is a covering layer, as of paint or fur.

clue.text: Perhaps saw something stolen being lifted

indicators.note: being lifted in a down answer means the word is read upwards

parts.note: loot is stolen goods

explanation.surface: Maybe someone saw stolen goods being stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is the cutting tool, an example, not the past of see; 'lifted' also hints at theft.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is one example of a hand tool.

clue.text: City that was cool in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish or cool
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A city that used to be fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major US city in Illinois.

clue.text: Wandering nomad read of stars

indicators.note: wandering sends the letters of nomad read roaming into a new order

explanation.surface: A travelling nomad reads about the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a named group of stars.

clue.text: Dress in which unit started training

parts.note: single means one unit

indicators.note: started takes the first letter of training

explanation.surface: Kit for a squad that began training.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest worn in sport, an item of clothing.
